name: Dr. Adnan Aminu Adnan
title: Associate Professor | Bio-Science Engineer | Founder CEO, ADAB Agri-Resources
bio:
DR. ADNAN AMINU ADNAN

Adnan is a multi-disciplinary leader with over 22 years of experience bridging the gap between agricultural science, commercial trade, and sustainable development across Nigeria, Ghana, Niger, Sierra Leone, Kenya, and Belgium.

A leading voice in the "Green Growth" transition, Adnan specializes in Nature-Based Solutions (NbS), Climate Finance and Climate-Smart Agriculture. As the Project Leader for Living Carbon Jigawa, he is at the forefront of creating low-carbon agro-commodity value chains and carbon trading frameworks. He provides strategic counsel to governments and development partners on transitioning smallholder farmers and SMEs into regenerative, traceable, and climate-resilient ecosystems. He currently advises the MD of Nigeria's Bank of Agriculture on Climate Finance. As the Founder and CEO of ADAB Agri-Resources Limited, Adnan leads a diversified agribusiness powerhouse specializing in large-scale crop production, commodity aggregation for export, and consultancy. As co-founder of ZeroBola, he leads a pragmatic project around agritech and Envirotech and how to create business out of deeptech in Nigeria.

Currently an Associate Professor at Bayero University Kano and the immediate past Deputy Director at the Centre for Dryland Agriculture (CDA), Adnan's research focuses on sustainable agriculture, backward integration and the traceability of export crops. He holds a PhD in Bio-Science Engineering from KU Leuven (Belgium), an MSc in Agronomy from Bayero University Kano, and a BSc in Plant Physiology from University of Maiduguri.

name: Chavala Yaduma
title: Filmmaker
bio:
CHAVALA YADUMA

Chavala Yaduma is a Nigerian filmmaker and artist passionate about storytelling that highlights social justice. She is also dedicated to advocacy through her work and leads a production company supporting young creatives.

name: Dr. Umar Ibrahim Dahiru
title: Development Economist | State Coordinator, NG-CARES Programme, Nasarawa State
bio:
DR. UMAR IBRAHIM DAHIRU

Umar Ibrahim Dahiru is a development economist, public-sector transformation leader, and advocate for inclusive development. He serves as the State Coordinator of the NG-CARES Programme in Nasarawa State, Nigeria, where he has helped drive institutional reforms that moved the state from 27th to first place nationally in programme performance, securing ₦52 billion in performance-based grants and impacting over 900,000 citizens, particularly poor and vulnerable populations.

Dahiru holds a PhD in Economics, which examined how community-driven development can advance social inclusion and empower vulnerable populations. Through his work with the Nasarawa Investment and Development Agency (NASIDA), he has contributed to investment promotion, ease-of-doing-business reforms, and initiatives to strengthen the state's economic competitiveness through public-private partnerships. His professional development includes awards and distinctions, as well as specialised training, study tours, and certifications from internationally recognised institutions, including Cambridge Judge Business School and Yale University.

His work spans economic development, business reforms, social protection, and community-driven development, giving him a perspective on how leadership and human relationships can influence decisions, unlock potential, and create opportunities for change. He is passionate about building effective, results-driven institutions that ensure public policies translate into meaningful improvements in people's lives.

name: Kauthar
title: Associate, DalaHill Law Practice
bio:
KAUTHAR

Kauthar is an Associate at DalaHill Law Practice, a corporate and commercial law firm in Abuja, advising on corporate governance, regulatory compliance, commercial transactions, and legal research. She acts for businesses, government entities, and entrepreneurs, helping them navigate complex legal and regulatory environments with practical, well-reasoned solutions.

Kauthar holds an LL.B. from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, and a B.L. from the Nigerian Law School. She is a member of the Nigerian Bar Association and a Chartered Mediator and Conciliator, a qualification that informs her collaborative, solutions-focused approach to dispute prevention and resolution.

Intellectually curious, Kauthar is drawn to differing perspectives and brings nuance and clarity to every matter. Her guiding philosophy is simple: leave things better than you found them. Whether she is asking the right questions, untangling a difficult problem, or finding a more practical way forward, she is committed to making a meaningful difference.

Outside the law, she believes that purpose and professionalism need not come at the expense of joy, and she makes room for laughter, kindness, and the small things that make life worthwhile.

name: Justice Muhammed Abdullahi Liman, JCA (rtd.)
title: Chairman, Policy Advisory Committee on National Policing Bill | Retired Justice of the Court of Appeal, Nigeria
bio:
JUSTICE MUHAMMED ABDULLAHI LIMAN, JCA (RTD.)

Justice Muhammed Abdullahi Liman is a distinguished Nigerian jurist with over four decades of experience in legal practice and judicial service. Born on 11 February 1959 in Lafia, Nasarawa State, he obtained his L.L.B from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, in 1983 and was called to the Nigerian Bar in 1984. He began his legal career in private practice after earlier serving in local government administration, before his appointment as a Judge of the Federal High Court in July 2000.

He later rose to the Court of Appeal, where he served as a Justice until his retirement, earning a reputation for judicial independence, constitutional interpretation, and the adjudication of high-profile electoral, commercial and public law matters. Throughout his career, Justice Liman has been recognised for his extensive judicial experience and contributions to Nigeria's legal system.

name: Jerry Ombugadu Musa
title: Junior Partner, J-K Gadzama LLP
talk_title: What If I Am Wrong About Myself?
bio:
JERRY OMBUGADU MUSA

Jerry Ombugadu Musa, a proud native of Nasarawa State, is a Junior Partner at J-K Gadzama LLP, one of Nigeria's leading law firms. His practice spans dispute resolution, corporate advisory, tax, and leisure sector law, such as sport and entertainment. Called in the year 2014, he holds an LL.M. from Nasarawa State University (where he's currently a PhD candidate) and has contributed to drafting key national legislation, including the 1999 Constitution (as amended), the Nigerian Evidence Act, the Fiscal Responsibility Act, and the Administration of Criminal Justice Act.

Beyond the courtroom, Jerry is a passionate teacher and discusser who finds deep joy in exploring law, faith, and the profound questions that shape human life. He believes that the most transformative moments often begin with simply accepting or accommodating uncomfortable questions, the kind that makes us pause and wonder if we have been telling ourselves the wrong story all along. His talk, "What If I Am Wrong About Myself?", invites the audience to examine the assumptions and limitations they have accepted as fact, and to discover the freedom and/or progress that comes when we dare to question them.

name: Saleh Barde Keana
title: Executive Chairman, Nasarawa State Disability Rights Commission (NSDRC)
bio:
SALEH BARDE KEANA

Saleh Barde Keana is a politician, disability rights advocate, academic and the pioneer Executive Chairman of the Nasarawa State Disability Rights Commission (NSDRC). Born on January 1, 1987, he has focused his career on advancing social inclusion, policy formulation, and equal opportunities for persons with disabilities (PWDs).

He graduated at the top of his class with a Second Class Upper Division in Psychology from Nasarawa State University, Keffi, and he is currently studying Clinical Psychology. Alongside his public service, he is a lecturer at the Federal University of Lafia (FULafia), where he is impacting knowledge in his field.

Saleh served as Personal Assistant in the Governor's Office (2016–2018), inaugural APC State Leader of Persons with Disabilities (2018), and Director of Special Interest Groups for the 2023 Campaign Council. Appointed NSDRC Chairman in 2024 by Governor Abdullahi A. Sule, his leadership is creating measurable impact by strengthening institutional frameworks, expanding digital and economic opportunities, and fostering equal rights.

A frequent speaker and participant at the national disability rights conferences, he regularly collaborates with government institutions, development partners, civil society organizations, and international NGOs to champion inclusive governance and lay a foundation for the long-held dream of an inclusive society.

He is married to Halima, and blessed with a son.

name: Hauwa Nana Ibrahim
title: Group Director, Non-Tax Revenue, Nigeria Revenue Service
bio:
HAUWA NANA IBRAHIM

Hauwa Nana Ibrahim is Group Director, Non-Tax Revenue at the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS). She oversees Nigeria's non-tax revenue streams, including petroleum and solid minerals royalties, levies and incentives, and is building the Non-Tax Revenue Group from the ground up following the country's 2025 tax reforms.

She began her career in 2009 as a Youth Corps member at Zenith Bank in Kano. She went on to work with Etisalat, GTBank and TotalEnergies before spending about a decade at NNPC (in its retail downstream operations). There she was the pioneer Regional Accountant and pioneer Financial Secretary of the Staff Cooperative Society, which she later led as President.

She then joined the Federal Inland Revenue Service as a Senior Tax Manager in the Special Tax Crimes Department. In 2023 she was appointed Special Adviser to the Honourable Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy. In that role she advised on revenue and debt management and led the secretariat for the Naira-for-Crude policy, under which Nigerian crude is sold to domestic refineries in naira.

She is a chartered accountant: a Fellow of ACCA, a member of ICAN and an associate of CITN. She holds a degree in Accounting from Ahmadu Bello University, an MSc in Professional Accountancy from the University of London (UCL), and Public Leadership Credentials from Harvard Kennedy School.

She is an alumna of the World Economic Forum's Global Shapers Community and a trained Climate Reality Leader. She has long mentored young people and is now building the Habaka Foundation to support individuals and communities through skills, mentorship and grants.

Northern by birth and national by duty, she is a mother of four.
